title: Philemon Bible Quiz - Chapter 1
description: Ten questions on Philemon 1: the greeting to Philemon and the assembly in his house, the plea for Onesimus, and the promise to repay what he owes.

questions.text: Who is named with Paul in the opening verse as "our brother"?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 names Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, as the senders of the letter.

questions.text: How is Philemon described in the first verse?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 calls Philemon "our beloved fellow worker".

answers.text: As an elder of the city

questions.text: What is Archippus called in verse 2?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 greets Apphia the beloved, and Archippus "our fellow soldier", and the assembly in the house.

questions.text: What had Paul heard about Philemon?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says he had heard of Philemon's love and of the faith which he had toward the Lord Jesus and toward all the saints.

questions.text: What has happened to the hearts of the saints through Philemon?
questions.explanation: Verse 7 says there is much joy and comfort in his love, because the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through him.

questions.text: Though he has boldness to command, what does Paul do instead for love's sake?
questions.explanation: Verses 8 and 9 say that although he has all boldness in Christ to command what is appropriate, for love's sake he rather begs.

questions.text: For whom does Paul beg, the child he became the father of in his chains?
questions.explanation: Verse 10 says he begs for his child Onesimus, whom he became the father of in his chains.

questions.text: How does verse 11 describe the change in Onesimus?
questions.explanation: Verse 11 says that he once was useless to Philemon, but now is useful to Philemon and to Paul.

answers.text: He was poor, but is now rich
He was silent, but now speaks
He was useless, but is now useful
He was far off, but is now near

questions.text: As what, rather than as a slave, should Philemon now have him?
questions.explanation: Verse 16 says he should have him no longer as a slave, but more than a slave, as a beloved brother.

answers.text: As a stranger in his house

questions.text: What does Paul say about anything Onesimus owes or any wrong he has done?
questions.explanation: Verses 18 and 19 say to put it to Paul's account, and that he writes with his own hand that he will repay it.

answers.text: That he will repay it himself
That the assembly will pay it
That it will be judged later
